items.title: Avakian George — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Even then I wondered, gee, how can they keep together? Sonny Greer was usually on the left side as you looked at the band.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, Hodges, Carney, and Bigard. The usual rhythm section with Freddie Guy. I guess at that time it was only Billy Taylor on bass. I think Wellman Braud had left, but I remember the band with the two basses, which by the way was a terrific sight,

to go to a theater and see the band come up on the elevator, literally, stage, which would rise out of the pit. The first thing you’d see in the dim light would be the two bass players at the opposite ends. Even then I wondered, gee, how can they keep together? Sonny Greer was usually on the left side as you looked at the band. But there were the two basses coming up first, and then this ghostly band would come up, and they’d be playing East St. Louis Toodle-oo. It was terrific. The spotlight would finally come…
This is interrupting your sequence, but I wonder, that kind of an experience for young people and for those who – everyone wasn’t young – but that’s missing today, isn’t it?
